title: Add option for local research tracker (#16)
description:
Add a local JSONL-based research tracker as an alternative to the Notion backend, so users without Notion (or without admin rights to create Notion integrations) can use McBrain's research workflow. Adds two new skills (local-research-db, local-research-runner) bundled with the plugin, generalizes mcbrain-setup Step 8 to choose a backend, and updates the CLAUDE.md template with a unified '## Research tracker' section. Findings flow through the existing raw/notes/ pipeline so no engine changes are needed.

Source: GitHub Issue jbdamask/McBrain#16

Plan: .plan/16-add-option-for-local-research-tracker.md

- All eight critical files listed in the plan's 'Critical Files' section have been created or modified per the plan.
- No engine MCP code is changed (notion.py, mcbrain_engine.py, registry.py untouched).
- plugins/mcbrain/skills/mcbrain/SKILL.md is unmodified (no third ingest mode added).
- pytest tests/test_local_research.py passes all four tests, including test_jsonl_atomic_concurrent_writers.
- Typecheck passes

title: Create local-research-runner/references/atomic_write_protocol.md
description:
Create plugins/mcbrain/skills/local-research-runner/references/atomic_write_protocol.md as a standalone reference document. Content is a verbatim copy of the 'Atomic Update Strategy' section from the plan (.plan/16-add-option-for-local-research-tracker.md), formatted as a contributor-facing reference.

Required content:
- The two-stdlib-primitive approach (exclusive-create lock + write-temp-then-os.replace).
- 'Why both' rationale.
- 'Why not other approaches' rationale (fcntl/flock CLI, msvcrt, TTL-based reclaim, PID liveness, O_APPEND, SQLite, third-party packages).
- The concrete protocol pseudocode (ACQUIRE_LOCK, READ, MODIFY, WRITE, RELEASE_LOCK) with the 5-second acquire timeout and 0.1s poll interval.
- Stuck-lock recovery instructions (no automatic reclaim, manual delete of tasks.jsonl.lock after confirming no other runner active).
- 'What this protects vs does NOT protect' summary including network-mount and Windows file-share-mode caveats.

This file is referenced from local-research-runner/SKILL.md so any contributor adding new write paths follows the same flow.

Source: GitHub Issue jbdamask/McBrain#16

Acceptance Criteria:
- The file plugins/mcbrain/skills/local-research-runner/references/atomic_write_protocol.md exists.
- Contains pseudocode for ACQUIRE_LOCK, READ, MODIFY, WRITE, RELEASE_LOCK.
- Mentions os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY for the lock acquire call.
- Mentions os.replace as the atomic-rename primitive.
- States the 5-second acquire timeout and the manual-recovery instruction (no automatic reclaim).
- Lists the 'What this protects vs does NOT protect' bullets including the network-mount and Windows file-share-mode caveats.
- Cross-platform constraint stated: works on macOS, Linux, and Windows using only Python stdlib (no fcntl, no msvcrt branching).
- Typecheck passes

title: Create local-research-db/SKILL.md
description:
Create plugins/mcbrain/skills/local-research-db/SKILL.md, modeled on the existing plugins/mcbrain/skills/notion-research-db/SKILL.md but adapted for the local backend.

Key differences from the Notion sibling:
- No Notion connector check, no parent-page selection, no integration token.
- Inputs: research topic (free-form string); McBrain vault (resolved via the same mcbrain-* MCP enumeration logic — copy the 'Identifying the McBrain vault' section verbatim from notion-research-db/SKILL.md).
- Workflow:
  1. Resolve vault, derive <topic-slug> (lowercase, hyphenated) from the topic.
  2. Ensure <vault>/raw/research_tasks/ exists. Ensure <vault>/raw/research_tasks/tasks.jsonl exists (touch if missing — empty file is valid).
  3. Register the topic in CLAUDE.md under a '## Research tracker' section with Backend: local, File: raw/research_tasks/tasks.jsonl, and a Topics: sublist entry. If the section already exists with Backend: local, append the new topic under Topics: instead of overwriting. If Backend: notion, surface the conflict to the user and ask whether to switch the backend or keep both registered.
  4. Append to wiki/log.md: '- YYYY-MM-DD — registered local tracker topic: <topic>'.
  5. Backup: same git/google-drive/none copy-paste-fence pattern as notion-research-db. The git commit fence is: 'git add CLAUDE.md raw/research_tasks/tasks.jsonl && git commit -m "init: local research tracker (<topic>)" && git push'.

The SKILL.md MUST include a 'Row schema' subsection that lists every JSONL field with a one-line description: id, topic, topic_slug, task_name, status, priority, created_date, last_updated_date, notes, notes_path, sources_count. This is what tests/test_local_research.py::test_jsonl_schema_documented parses.

Idempotency: running the skill twice with the same topic is a no-op (jsonl already exists; CLAUDE.md entry detected as already-present).

Source: GitHub Issue jbdamask/McBrain#16

Depends on the claude-md-template.md update (defines the '## Research tracker' contract this skill writes).

Acceptance Criteria:

title: Create local-research-runner/SKILL.md
description:
Create plugins/mcbrain/skills/local-research-runner/SKILL.md, modeled on plugins/mcbrain/skills/notion-research-runner/SKILL.md with the same Phase 1-5 shape, adapted for the local JSONL backend.

Differences from the Notion runner:
- No Notion-connector capability matching at startup.
- Inputs: topic to drain (resolve via '## Research tracker -> Topics' in CLAUDE.md; ask if multiple topics are registered and the user did not specify); batch size (default 5, hard cap 5).

Phases:
- Phase 1 — Fetch candidates: Acquire the lock; read raw/research_tasks/tasks.jsonl; filter rows where topic_slug == <selected> AND status == 'To do'; sort by priority (High -> Medium -> Low) then created_date ascending; take the first N. Lock is held through Phase 2.
- Phase 2 — Claim: Following the atomic protocol — set status = 'In progress' and last_updated_date = <now ISO-8601> on each claimed row, write all rows (claimed and unclaimed) to a tempfile in raw/research_tasks/, fsync, os.replace over the original, release the lock.
- Phase 3 — Plan + research: Reuse references/research_subagent_prompt.md verbatim. Spawn one general-purpose subagent per claimed task in a single message (parallel). Subagents do NOT touch tasks.jsonl; they return findings markdown to the runner.
- Phase 4 — Write findings then update JSONL: For each subagent return: (a) write the markdown file at <vault>/raw/notes/research-<topic-slug>-<task-id>.md with the frontmatter block (source, topic, topic_slug, task_id, task_name, research_date, captured) followed by the verbatim subagent output. (b) Atomically update the JSONL row: acquire lock, read, find row by id, set notes_path, sources_count (parsed best-effort from Sources section; leave unset on parse failure), bump last_updated_date, set status = 'Done', write+rename, release lock. Each task gets its own lock cycle in Phase 4 — do NOT batch updates.
- Phase 5 — Report: per-task title, one-line takeaway pulled from '## Summary' of the markdown file, the row id, and the markdown path.

Failure modes (mirror the Notion runner section):
- Subagent malformed output -> do NOT write the markdown file, do NOT flip status; row stays at 'In progress' for retry on next run.
- Runner killed between writing markdown and updating JSONL -> markdown exists but row is 'In progress' with empty notes_path. On next run, detect this and offer to reconcile.
- Runner killed mid-claim (Phase 2) -> orphaned lock file may remain; rows stay at 'To do'; next runner surfaces the 5-second-timeout 'delete the .lock file manually' message.

Troubleshooting section MUST mention the stuck-lock recovery instruction (delete tasks.jsonl.lock manually after confirming no other runner is active) so users do not have to grep the plan.

The SKILL.md must include or references/-link the atomic protocol so an implementing contributor cannot accidentally do a non-atomic update. Reference references/atomic_write_protocol.md.

Prerequisites note: 'Python 3.x available locally'. Single-machine assumption (out of scope: two runners on different machines pointing at the same vault path).

Source: GitHub Issue jbdamask/McBrain#16

Depends on T2 (atomic_write_protocol.md) and T3 (research_subagent_prompt.md).

Acceptance Criteria:
- The file plugins/mcbrain/skills/local-research-runner/SKILL.md exists with valid frontmatter (name, description).
- The five-phase workflow is present (Fetch, Claim, Plan+research, Write+update, Report) and matches the descriptions above.
- Phase 4 explicitly states each task gets its own lock cycle (no batching).
- The Troubleshooting section instructs the user to delete tasks.jsonl.lock manually after confirming no other runner is active.
- The 'Row schema' subsection lists all 11 fields (id, topic, topic_slug, task_name, status, priority, created_date, last_updated_date, notes, notes_path, sources_count).
- The SKILL.md links references/atomic_write_protocol.md and references/research_subagent_prompt.md.
- The markdown filename convention 'research-<topic-slug>-<task-id>.md' is documented.
- The frontmatter block fields (source, topic, topic_slug, task_id, task_name, research_date, captured) are documented.
- The SKILL.md does NOT mention Notion connectors as a required prerequisite.
- Typecheck passes

title: Update mcbrain-setup/SKILL.md Step 8 to choose research-tracker backend

Changes:
1. New 8a — Choose research-tracker backend. Use AskUserQuestion with three options:
   - 'Local (Recommended — no Notion needed)' — JSONL file at raw/research_tasks/, zero deps, works offline.
   - 'Notion' — Notion DB; needs a Notion MCP connector and admin rights.
   - 'Skip for now' — none; user can add later.
   Store the choice as RESEARCH_TRACKER_BACKEND ∈ {local, notion, none}.

2. 8L — Local backend branch (only if local). Steps:
   - Touch <vault>/raw/research_tasks/tasks.jsonl using the Write tool against the granted vault mount.
   - Append a '## Research tracker' section to CLAUDE.md with Backend: local, the File: line, and one entry under Topics: (per the template). Default topic should be a sensible name derived from the vault domain.
   - No Notion token, no MCP-engine call (the engine does not need to know about local trackers).
   - If git backup is configured, present a single copy-paste commit fence: 'git add CLAUDE.md raw/research_tasks/tasks.jsonl && git commit -m "init: local research tracker" && git push'.

3. 8N — Notion backend branch (only if notion). This is today's 8a-8g flow renumbered. The token install (today's 8f) and the enable_notion_for_vault call (today's Step 8.5) are gated to this branch.

4. Update the 'Required intake' table at the top of SKILL.md so row 8 becomes 'RESEARCH_TRACKER_BACKEND ∈ {local, notion, none}'.

5. Step 8.5's enable_notion_for_vault call becomes conditional on RESEARCH_TRACKER_BACKEND == notion.

Recommend 'local' as the default in the AskUserQuestion options copy because it has zero dependencies.

title: Add tests/test_local_research.py with mandatory concurrency test
description:
Create tests/test_local_research.py with four tests covering the JSONL schema, the Phase 2 + Phase 4 round trip, concurrent writers, and the CLAUDE.md template change.

The two new skills are pure markdown so they don't import the way engine code does. The JSONL schema and the atomic-rewrite logic are testable in pure Python.

Tests:

1. test_jsonl_schema_documented — read both new SKILL.md files (local-research-db, local-research-runner) and assert each lists every required field: id, topic, topic_slug, task_name, status, priority, created_date, last_updated_date, notes, notes_path, sources_count.

2. test_runner_claim_then_findings_round_trip — minimal Python helper inline in the test (NOT in the skill) that simulates Phase 2 + Phase 4 against a fixture tasks.jsonl: load -> claim 3 rows -> verify atomic rewrite (temp file gone, rename worked, other rows untouched) -> 'complete' them by writing markdown files and updating rows -> verify status, notes_path, last_updated_date are correct.

3. test_jsonl_atomic_concurrent_writers — MANDATORY hard gate. Spawn 5 subprocesses that simultaneously try to claim 3 rows each from a fixture tasks.jsonl containing 30 'To do' rows. Each subprocess uses the documented exclusive-create lock (os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY) + temp-rename (os.replace) protocol. Assertions:
   (a) Total claimed rows across all subprocesses = 15 (each row claimed exactly once — no double-claims, no lost claims).
   (b) tasks.jsonl parses as valid JSONL after all subprocesses exit (no truncation, no interleaved bytes).
   (c) Row count is unchanged (30 rows in, 30 rows out).
   (d) Every row that ended up 'In progress' has a last_updated_date newer than the fixture's original timestamps.
   (e) The lock file (tasks.jsonl.lock) does NOT exist after all subprocesses exit cleanly (it is unlinked on lock release).

4. test_claude_md_template_has_research_tracker_section — assert the template plugins/mcbrain/skills/mcbrain-setup/references/claude-md-template.md now has '## Research tracker' with 'Backend:' and (when local) 'File:' lines, and that the legacy '## Notion companion databases' heading is either gone or clearly marked as the old name.

Use only Python stdlib (subprocess, multiprocessing, os, json, tempfile, time, datetime, pathlib). No new pip dependencies.

Source: GitHub Issue jbdamask/McBrain#16

Depends on T1 (template change), T4 and T5 (SKILL files for schema-documented test).

Acceptance Criteria:
- The file tests/test_local_research.py exists.
- pytest tests/test_local_research.py collects 4 tests.
- All 4 tests pass: test_jsonl_schema_documented, test_runner_claim_then_findings_round_trip, test_jsonl_atomic_concurrent_writers, test_claude_md_template_has_research_tracker_section.
- The concurrency test spawns exactly 5 subprocesses against a 30-row fixture and asserts all five conditions (a)-(e) above.
- The test file imports only from the Python stdlib (no third-party packages).
- Tests pass
- Typecheck passes
